title: R2 v3: orchestrator/capacity.py — read-only capacity snapshot and deterministic admission with reservation only for imminent higher-priority demand (AP P6)
spec:
Why: daemon.free_slots (orchestrator/daemon.py:449-465) reduces capacity to one integer, so waves ignore per-task executor eligibility and premium capacity can go to low-impact work while a critical-path task is about to become ready (AP P6; brief P3). v3 after spec reviews T-0566 and T-0588.
What: new pure module orchestrator/capacity.py; never mutates the pool; no daemon edits. Tests: this repo runs unittest; every acceptance test id is a `def test_name(self)` method inside a unittest.TestCase subclass in that file; no pytest fixtures.
- snapshot(pool, running_claude=0, inflight_claude=0, now=None) -> {"executors": {id: {"free": max(0, max_parallel - running), "cooling_s": max(0, cooldown_until - now), "enabled", "roles", "complexity": [complexity_min, complexity_max], "day_tasks_left", "weight"}}, "claude_workers_free": max(0, limits.max_parallel_claude_workers - running_claude - inflight_claude), "accounts": {id: {"utilization", "cooling_s"}}, "fallback": every enabled execute executor is cooling, "ts": now}.
  day_tasks_left = None if daily_budget_tasks == 0 (0 means unlimited, pool.py:533 convention) else daily_budget_tasks - effective_day_tasks, where effective_day_tasks = ex.day_tasks if ex.day == today (today = datetime.fromtimestamp(now).astimezone().date().isoformat(), the same comparison Executor.roll_day uses) else 0.
  utilization = (acct.window_tokens + acct.planner_window_tokens) / cap if now - acct.window_started <= pool.WINDOW_S else 0.0, with cap = the account's window_cap_tokens from pool cfg; day tokens play no role (they only matter for the rollover Account.utilization performs as a side effect, which snapshot must never trigger). Account and Executor objects are read, never called for utilization/roll_day, never written.
- eligible_executors_from_snapshot(task, snapshot) -> executor ids with 'execute' in roles, enabled, cooling_s == 0, complexity_min <= task complexity <= complexity_max, free > 0, day_tasks_left None or > 0. In fallback mode returns ['claude'] when pool.fallback_tier(task complexity) is not None, else [].
- admit(ranked_ids, tasks, snapshot, priorities, imminent=None, cfg=None) -> {"admit": [ids], "deferred": {id: reason}, "assignments": {id: executor_id}, "reasons": {id: text}}. Two phases. Phase 1 (imminent demand): imminent is a list of task ids that are NOT ready yet but whose every depends_on is merged or is status done with pipeline.gated_at set (the caller computes this from the bus; the daemon integration will pass it); for each imminent task Z with priority['critical_path_s'] greater than that of a ranked candidate, compute Z's eligible executor set from the snapshot. Phase 2 walks ranked_ids in order: pick the eligible executor with the most free capacity, then lowest weight; before assigning candidate X to executor E, if some imminent Z with higher priority has E as its ONLY eligible executor and E has exactly one free slot left, defer X with reason reserved_for_critical:<Z> unless X has no other eligible executor and no imminent task is blocked... (rule: X is deferred only when an alternative executor exists for neither X nor Z; if X has another eligible executor, assign that one instead). Decrement a local copy of free. With imminent empty or None, phase 1 is skipped and nothing is ever reserved.
  Reasons: executor_capacity (eligible set non-empty but no free slot), cooldown (only cooling executors would match), account_capacity (fallback mode, claude_workers_free exhausted), budget (only day_tasks_left == 0 executors would match), reserved_for_critical:<id>, no_eligible_executor (complexity range or role excludes every executor). cfg [scheduler] reserve_imminent = true (default; false disables phase 1).
- priorities: {task_id: critical_path.explain dict}; ranked_ids already ordered by the caller (critical path first).
acceptance: tests/test_capacity.py::test_snapshot_is_read_only_across_day_and_window_rollover — an executor whose day is yesterday with day_tasks 5 and daily_budget_tasks 5 reports day_tasks_left 5; an account whose window_started is older than WINDOW_S reports utilization 0.0; no attribute of the pool, accounts or executors changes across the call
tests/test_capacity.py::test_unlimited_daily_budget_reports_none — daily_budget_tasks 0 with day_tasks 7 today reports day_tasks_left None and stays eligible
tests/test_capacity.py::test_executor_full_defers_with_executor_capacity_reason — every eligible executor at max_parallel yields deferred reason executor_capacity
tests/test_capacity.py::test_quota_cooling_executor_is_not_eligible — a cooling executor is excluded and a task only it could run is deferred with reason cooldown
tests/test_capacity.py::test_account_fallback_uses_claude_worker_headroom — fallback snapshot admits at most claude_workers_free tasks and defers the rest with account_capacity

tests/test_capacity.py::test_imminent_critical_task_reserves_last_slot — an imminent higher-priority task whose only eligible executor has one free slot causes a lower-priority candidate with no alternative executor to be deferred with reserved_for_critical naming it, while a candidate that has an alternative executor is assigned there instead

tests/test_capacity.py::test_idle_capacity_admits_everything_and_no_unnecessary_reservation — with spare capacity and imminent None every ready task is admitted and no reserved_for_critical reason appears

constraints.interface_contract: snapshot(pool, running_claude=0, inflight_claude=0, now=None) -> dict as specified, read-only; eligible_executors_from_snapshot(task, snapshot) -> ids; admit(ranked_ids, tasks, snapshot, priorities, imminent=None, cfg=None) -> {admit, deferred, assignments, reasons}; reason vocabulary executor_capacity|cooldown|account_capacity|budget|reserved_for_critical:<id>|no_eligible_executor; config [scheduler].reserve_imminent default true; module must not import daemon
